gayā.notes: Gayā 02 is the town on Upaka’s route in MN 26:25.1. Its discussion of bathing places belongs with the town’s history. DPPN has a separate Gayā 1 for the bathing pond, absent from the packet. MN 7:20.2–6 lists Gayā among places to bathe. Ud 1.9:1.2–3 uses gayāyaṁ first for the Buddha’s location and then for the water the ascetics plunge into. The page lookup also picks up AN 8.63 and SN 35.27. The town occurs in AN 8.64 and SN 35.28. AN 8.70:22.2 is a chapter recap.

gayākassapa.notes: The speaker of Thag 5.7 recalls bathing three times daily at the Gayā festival. The closing attribution names Gayākassapa. The packet misses Thag 5.12:6.4, where the chapter recap pairs him with Vakkalī in gayākassapavakkalī. Tapping that form gives his DPD line.

gayāsīsa.notes: SN 35.28:1.1 places the Buddha and a thousand monks on the hill at Gayā for the fire discourse. SN 35.27 shares the cited page and gives no location.

gaṅgā.notes: The zero mention count is an English-filter error. Forms such as gaṅgā and gaṅgāya also have the ordinary sense ‘river’, and Sujato calls the named river ‘Ganges’. AN 8.19:5.2 lists it with the other four great rivers, MN 34:1.2 places the Buddha on its bank, and AN 3.100:4.7 puts salt in it. The DPD hint AN 3.101 is the gold panner in this corpus. SN 13.5, SN 22.94, SN 35.240 and SN 35.245 are neighboring discourses included by the page lookup.

gaṇakamoggallāna.notes: MN 107 names the accountant at 1.3 and records his taking refuge at 17.4. Correct the DPD example to MN 107. MN 108 is Ānanda’s conversation with Gopaka Moggallāna.

ghaṭīkāra.notes: The deity in SN 2.24:1.1 identifies himself at 9.1–4 as the former potter who supported his parents and followed Buddha Kassapa. MN 81:6.1 spells the potter’s name ghaṭikāro, which has its own DPD lemma. SN 1.50:8.2 spells it ghaṭīkaro, which yields the occupational gloss alone. Both passages belong to this biography. SN 1.49 shares the cited page with SN 1.50.

ghositārāma.notes: MN 48:1.2 places the Kosambī dispute at Ghosita’s monastery. Check DPPN’s inclusion of the Sekhasutta among discourses delivered there. MN 53:1.2 places it at Nigrodha’s monastery in Kapilavatthu. The visit to the sick nun is AN 4.159. AN 7.43 concerns Ānanda’s visit to wanderers. The page lookup also includes AN 3.71, MN 47 and SN 12.67. The monastery is named in AN 3.72, MN 48 and SN 12.68 respectively.

ghoṭamukha.notes: MN 94 identifies him through his conversation with Udena and the hall he builds at Pāṭaliputta. MN 93 concerns Assalāyana and shares the cited page. The English filter misses MN 94:33.9, where the Pali names Ghoṭamukha and the English uses ‘he’. MN 100:44.2 also names him in the chapter recap.

gijjhakūṭa.notes: SN 35.87:1.2 places Channa, Sāriputta and Cunda on Vulture’s Peak. Distinguish the neighboring citations for the spirits. SN 10.1 places Indaka on Indakūṭa, SN 10.2 places the spirit called Sakka on Gijjhakūṭa, and SN 10.3 places Suciloma at Gayā. Other page overlaps include MN 73/74, MN 143/144, SN 35.86/87 and SN 56.41/42. In each pair the second discourse names the peak.

gopaka.notes: In DN 21:1.11.5–12 Sakka recounts how the Sakyan woman Gopikā was reborn as the god Gopaka and rebuked the former monks.

gopakamoggallāna.notes: MN 108:3.4 identifies the brahmin at whose workplace Ānanda stops. At 6.2 the text calls Vassakāra the minister inspecting the works. MN 107 concerns Gaṇaka Moggallāna. DPPN also attributes the 84,000 teachings verse to Moggallāna Thera. In the corpus it is Ānanda’s verse (Thag 17.3:11), and the verse names no questioner.

gopāla.notes: DN 32:10.1 introduces the yakkhas and their generals one can call on for help. Gopāla appears in that list at 10.14 and in its repetition at 12.263.

gosiṅgasālavanadāya.notes: DPD points to MN 31, where the Buddha goes from the brick house at Ñātika to visit Anuruddha, Nandiya and Kimbila. MN 32 matches the same entry’s account of Sāriputta and the elders discussing who would grace the grove. AN 10.72 matches the second entry’s account of Cāla and his companions leaving the noisy gathering near Vesālī. The episodes identify the entries even though the texts leave open whether the groves were geographically distinct. MN 30 and AN 10.71 both open at Jetavana and are page overlaps.

gosālathera.notes: Thag 1.23 names Gosāla in the heading and attributes the verse to Gosālo thero at 1.7. The honeyed milk-rice and return to the hill match DPPN. The packet’s only mention, gosālathero at Thag 1.30:2.2, is in the chapter recap after Uttiya’s verse. The two-word attribution in Thag 1.23 uses the separate DPD sense gosāla 2.
